question: Who among the following chroniclers wrote his first chronicle in 1356?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ziyauddin Barani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ziyauddin Barani** was a notable chronicler and historian of the Delhi Sultanate period in India.
 
• He wrote his first chronicle, **"Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi"**, in 1356, which documented the history of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Barani served as a court historian under Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq and later under Firuz Shah Tughlaq.
 
• His writings reflect his Islamic perspective and provide valuable insights into the political, social, and economic aspects of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Barani emphasized the importance of Islamic governance and the role of religion in statecraft, often critiquing rulers for their deviation from Islamic principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi**

 
 
• This work is an essential source for understanding the Delhi Sultanate's history during the 13th and 14th centuries.
 
• It covers the reigns of rulers such as Ghiyasuddin Balban, Alauddin Khilji, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
 
• Barani’s chronicle provides detailed accounts of administration, military campaigns, and societal developments.
 
 
 
• **Minhaj-us-Siraj**
 
 
• An earlier historian who wrote **"Tabaqat-i-Nasiri"**, covering the history of Islamic rule in India up to 1260.
 
• His work is considered one of the most authentic sources for the early Delhi Sultanate period.
 
 
 
• **Al-Biruni**
 
 
• A renowned Persian scholar, Al-Biruni authored **"Kitab al-Hind"**, which focused on Indian culture, sciences, and religion during the early 11th century.
 
• He was associated with Mahmud of Ghazni and visited India during his invasions.
 
 
 
• **Ibn Sina (Avicenna)**
 
 
• A prominent Persian polymath known for his works on medicine, philosophy, and science, such as **"The Canon of Medicine."**
 
• His contributions were unrelated to the chronicle tradition of Indian history.
